scope.summary: Implement the BodyRecipe system per Section 13.25 (SREQ-001/002/019): BRC- recipes with save/load/diff/partial-apply and separable shape/skin/genital/physics layers — 'take her breasts, keep my face' as a first-class operation, with the direct-language phrasing preserved as the contract test name.
acceptance_criteria: BodyRecipe persists as a BRC- row: ordered channel values plus separable layer refs (shape / skin / genitals / physics), each layer independently loadable and swappable (SREQ-002).
save/load round-trips deterministically: loading a recipe onto a fresh base reproduces the identical BodySpec (hash equality).
diff(recipe_a, recipe_b) returns a typed per-channel and per-layer diff consumable by models and the GUI browser.

partial_apply with a region/layer scope copies only the scoped values: applying recipe B's breast-region channels onto body A changes ONLY breast channels — the take_her_breasts_keep_my_face test proves face and all other regions bit-identical.
Recipes are pure parameter sets (no mesh payload) so A/B snapshot and rollback are cheap (SREQ-023).

Owns selected application of hsk.tailor.character_sheet_body_mapping_proposal@1 through BodyRecipe partial-apply with explicit selected fields/layers, expected BodySpec base hash, actor/lease/event attribution, provenance, previewed diff, and deterministic replay.
Rejects stale, wrong-character, unknown-channel, unselected-field, or incompatible schema/version proposals without partial authority mutation.
scope.risk_if_missed: Characters are monoliths instead of composable parameter sets — no mixing the best tits with the best face, no cheap rollback, no recipe ecosystem — surrendering the single largest workflow advantage parametric bodies have over Daz.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit model and agent operation

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Extend BodyRecipe mix provenance for character-sheet mapping and selected apply; raw sheet text never enters solver state.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.

requirements: Resolve Principal, AuthenticatedSession and AccessSpace before every resource read or mutation.
Use PostgreSQL RLS/FORCE RLS and ResourceBroker-backed artifact/file handles; UI filtering is never the security boundary.
Derived resources preserve the intersection of source access scopes and must not leak existence through counts, search, previews, logs, traces, caches, diagnostics, exports or model context.
